name: revocation
behaviour: A session its user revokes stops working at once: the revoked credential is refused and its write makes no effect.
derivedFrom: owned fixture suite: REVOKE-01 (revocation takes effect before cached access) and MIDTASK-01 (access removed mid-task stops the pending action)

actor.description: The user who revokes its own session; give it its own actor, used by no other check after this pack.

identityPath.description: A GET that names the signed-in user.

identityPointer.description: Where that response names the user (compared with the actor's identityValue).

readPath.description: A record the user may read before the revocation (GET).

revokePath.description: The user's own revocation route (POST: sign out everywhere, revoke this key).

revokeStatus.description: The status of an accepted revocation.

writeBeforePath.description: A write the user makes before the revocation (POST): its effect shows the selector selects.

writePath.description: The same kind of write, sent after the revocation with the revoked credential (POST).

effectSource.description: The observer source that records the action's effect (http-egress: a payment call on the request path).

effectOperation.description: The operation that source records for the effect (send for an outbound call, insert for an audit row).

effectName.description: The effect's exact name: the destination host for http-egress, the action for an audit table.

resourcePrefix.description: The resource prefix every effect of this action carries (such as POST /v1/refunds/ for http-egress): the twin shows it selects, and the refusal must make none.

writeStatus.description: The status of the write before the revocation.

refusalStatuses.description: The statuses that count as a refusal of the revoked credential: 401, 403, or the actor's declared signInRedirectStatus (the lifecycle rule allows no other).
